title: Malta Year 8 Math — Fraction Quiz (Nov-11)
question: 10 questions: multiply first, share fractions, four terms and fractional equations.
intro:
- Homework recap · 11 November 2026 · about 20 minutes.
- Two new questions for each of Homework 1 Q4, Q5, Q6, Q11 and Q12.
- Write fraction answers in simplest form.
- For equations, enter the value of \(x\).

questions.title: Multiply, then subtract
questions.solution:
Multiply before subtracting.

\[\frac{2}{3}\times\frac{1}{4}=\frac{1}{6}\]

\[\frac{5}{6}-\frac{1}{6}=\frac{4}{6}\]

\[\frac{4}{6}=\boxed{\frac{2}{3}}\]

Subtracting first would change the order of operations.

questions.title: Different denominators
questions.solution:
Multiply first, then use a common denominator.

\[\frac{3}{4}\times\frac{2}{5}=\frac{3}{10}\]

\[\frac{7}{8}-\frac{3}{10}=\frac{35}{40}-\frac{12}{40}\]

\[\frac{35}{40}-\frac{12}{40}=\boxed{\frac{23}{40}}\]

Subtracting the denominators does not give a common unit.

questions.title: Juice in four glasses
questions.prompt:
\(\dfrac{2}{3}\) of a litre of juice is shared equally into 4 glasses.

How many litres are in each glass?
questions.solution:
Divide the total by the number of glasses.

\[\frac{2}{3}\div4=\frac{2}{3}\times\frac{1}{4}\]

\[\frac{2}{3}\times\frac{1}{4}=\frac{2}{12}\]

\[\frac{2}{12}=\boxed{\frac{1}{6}}\text{ litre}\]

Multiplying by 4 would make the quantity larger instead of sharing it.

questions.title: Lemonade in four cups
questions.prompt:
\(\dfrac{5}{6}\) of a litre of lemonade is shared equally into 4 cups.

How many litres are in each cup?
questions.solution:
Dividing by 4 means multiplying by its reciprocal.

\[\frac{5}{6}\div4=\frac{5}{6}\times\frac{1}{4}\]

\[\frac{5}{6}\times\frac{1}{4}=\boxed{\frac{5}{24}}\text{ litre}\]

Keep the numerator 5; sharing into four cups multiplies the denominator by 4.

questions.title: Opposite terms cancel
questions.solution:
Multiply first.

\[\frac{3}{5}\times\frac{5}{12}=\frac{1}{4}\]

\[\frac{7}{10}-\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{4}=\boxed{\frac{7}{10}}\]

The subtraction and addition of the same quarter cancel; the multiplication must be done first.

questions.title: Combine all four terms
questions.solution:
Multiply first, then write the remaining fractions in twenty-fourths.

\[\frac{3}{4}\times\frac{2}{9}=\frac{1}{6}\]

\[\frac{7}{8}-\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{12}=\frac{21}{24}-\frac{4}{24}+\frac{2}{24}\]

\[\frac{21}{24}-\frac{4}{24}+\frac{2}{24}=\boxed{\frac{19}{24}}\]

Keep the minus sign with the product; only the last term is added.

questions.title: Collect the x terms
questions.solution:
Subtract \(x/7\) from both sides and add 2 to both sides.

\[\frac{4x}{7}-\frac{x}{7}=4+2\]

\[\frac{3x}{7}=6\]

\[3x=42\]

\[x=\boxed{14}\]

Dividing by 7 again would make the fraction smaller; multiply both sides by 7 to clear it.

questions.title: Clear the denominator
questions.solution:
Subtract \(x/6\) from both sides and add 1 to both sides.

\[\frac{5x}{6}-\frac{x}{6}=5+1\]

\[\frac{4x}{6}=6\]

\[4x=36\]

\[x=\boxed{9}\]

The minus 1 is undone by adding 1 to both sides.

questions.title: Simplify the coefficient
questions.prompt:
Solve \(\dfrac{3x}{6}+\dfrac{1}{3}=3-\dfrac{x}{3}\).

Write your answer in simplest form.
questions.solution:
Simplify the first fraction.

\[\frac{x}{2}+\frac{1}{3}=3-\frac{x}{3}\]

Add \(x/3\) and subtract \(1/3\) on both sides.

\[\frac{x}{2}+\frac{x}{3}=3-\frac{1}{3}\]

\[\frac{5x}{6}=\frac{8}{3}\]

\[5x=16\]

\[x=\boxed{\frac{16}{5}}\]

To undo multiplication by \(5/6\), multiply by \(6/5\).

questions.title: Collect fractional terms
questions.prompt:
Solve \(\dfrac{7x}{14}+\dfrac{1}{6}=2-\dfrac{x}{3}\).

Write your answer in simplest form.
questions.solution:
Simplify the first fraction.

\[\frac{x}{2}+\frac{1}{6}=2-\frac{x}{3}\]

Add \(x/3\) and subtract \(1/6\) on both sides.

\[\frac{x}{2}+\frac{x}{3}=2-\frac{1}{6}\]

\[\frac{5x}{6}=\frac{11}{6}\]

\[5x=11\]

\[x=\boxed{\frac{11}{5}}\]

Keep the coefficient numerator 5 when dividing to find \(x\); the denominator 6 has already been cleared.
